method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: Scleroderma renal crisis: ACE inhibitors, hypertensive emergency, captopril
topic.coverageNote: Questions are limited to ACE-inhibitor choice, titration, and pregnancy.

mcqs.question: Which ACE inhibitor does the update prefer in pregnancy, and why?

options.A: Captopril, because of a lower risk of fetal renal complications
options.B: Ramipril, because it is long-acting and non-teratogenic
options.C: Enalapril, as the only ACE inhibitor studied
options.D: No ACE inhibitor may be used in pregnancy even if the mother is dying
options.E: Losartan is preferred to any ACE inhibitor

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Captopril, because of a lower risk of fetal renal complications
mcqs.explanation: In pregnancy, captopril is preferred because of a lower risk of fetal renal complications. The teratogenic risk is outweighed by the threat of renal crisis to the mother.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Captopril is the preferred choice due to lower risk of foetal renal complications. ACEi carries a teratogenic risk to the foetus but in this scenario, this is outweighed by the life-threatening complication of SRC to the mother.

mcqs.question: Which ACE inhibitor is most often used, and when is captopril suitable outside pregnancy?

options.A: A long-acting agent such as ramipril is most used; captopril may suit hemodynamic compromise
options.B: Captopril is mandatory in every outpatient
options.E: ACE inhibitors are interchangeable with beta-blockers as first-line

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A long-acting agent such as ramipril is most used; captopril may suit hemodynamic compromise
mcqs.explanation: A long-acting ACE inhibitor such as ramipril is most used, but short-acting captopril may be suitable when there is hemodynamic compromise.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A long-acting ACEi such as ramipril is most used but short-acting agents such as captopril may be suitable in cases of haemodynamic compromise.

mcqs.question: How is a long-acting ACE inhibitor titrated?

options.A: The dose is normally doubled at about 24-hour intervals
options.B: The dose is fixed and never increased
options.C: It is doubled every 15 minutes until creatinine normalizes
options.E: It is reduced by half each day

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The dose is normally doubled at about 24-hour intervals
mcqs.explanation: A long-acting agent is doubled at 24-hour intervals up toward the maximum dose. Adequate blood-pressure control often takes 3–5 days.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A long-acting agent is preferable in most cases as it can be easily up-titrated to maximum dose, normally by doubling the dose at 24-h intervals. Adequate control of blood pressure often takes 3–5 days.

mcqs.question: A patient with prior renal crisis is planning pregnancy. What does the update recommend about the ACE inhibitor?

options.A: Continue the ACE inhibitor during pregnancy and optimize blood pressure before conception
options.B: Stop it three months before conception in every case
options.D: Pregnancy is impossible after renal crisis
options.E: Continue it only in the third trimester

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Continue the ACE inhibitor during pregnancy and optimize blood pressure before conception
mcqs.explanation: For patients with a history of renal crisis who are planning pregnancy, the ACE inhibitor should continue and blood pressure should be optimized before conception, acknowledging teratogenic risk.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In patients with history of SRC planning a pregnancy, it is recommended that ACEi continue during the pregnancy and BP is optimised prior to conceiving.

mcqs.question: If the patient is already on an ACE inhibitor when crisis is recognized, what is the next dose change?

options.B: Stop it because it caused the crisis
options.D: Replace it with methyldopa as in historical practice

mcqs.explanation: If the patient is already taking an ACE inhibitor, the dose should be increased.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If the patient is already taking an ACEi, then the dose should be increased.
